title: When Jesus Claims the Sinner's Heart
description: When Jesus Claims the Sinner's Heart in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 84, “Satan returning. Mt 12:43-45”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When Je-sus claims the sin-ner's heart, Where Sa-tan ruled be-fore; The e-vil spir-it must de-part, And dares re-turn no more.

lines: When Jesus claims the sinner's heart,
But when he goes without constraint,
Some outward change perhaps is seen
But though the house seem swept and clean,
Except the Savior dwell and reign
No more by checks to be controlled,
The sinner's former state was bad,
He lives possessed, and blind, and mad,
Lord save me from this dreadful end!
And from this heart of mine,
O drive and keep away the fiend
Who fears no voice but thine.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
